scope: Friend invitations and collaborative album editing

passed: Owner sign-in and own album library
Owner opens saved album and generates a single-use HTTPS invite
Copy button reports success and HTTPS URL is visibly rendered
Owner member page exposes invite and unused-link cancellation controls
Logout, anonymous HTTPS invitation preview, login as another account, return to the same invite
Accept invitation, success state and open the shared album
Accepted editor can view private saved photos and open the editor
Add local text, save as another ordinary owner actor, display remote-change notice
Stale save opens explicit reload confirmation; keeping edits preserves local text
Permission revocation blocks saving and preserves local text in read-only UI
Read-only exit requires explicit discard confirmation
Reload a consumed invitation path with an album hash restores the reader without a new invite overlay
Fresh viewer reader hides edit and order actions
Final build: conflict, retain local edits, change role to VIEWER, automatic foreground check enters read-only mode without another save
Final build: local text remains visible after automatic permission revocation
Log out and return to anonymous feed
browser.clipboard_content_verification: The browser automation clipboard bridge returned an empty string. Only the visible HTTPS URL and success feedback are claimed.

decisions.collaborative_publication: New or republished collaborative snapshots are blocked until a participant-consent flow exists
decisions.editing: Whole-document revision checks and 15-second foreground status checks; no implicit overwrite or automatic merge

limitations: No physical phone was available. The debug APK is built and verified but physical-device installation and operation were not tested.
Previously issued signed URLs remain usable until expiry; already downloaded images cannot be recalled.
Accepted collaboration history is retained going forward. Membership removed before this migration cannot be reconstructed.
Initial album creation still uses the existing INSERT transport. This verification does not certify deduplication when the initial creation response is lost.
